text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 1.66% today to close at $484.92, continuing a strong two-week rally of 22.6%. The climb reflects sustained strength in crude oil prices—US oil is trading at $96.24 per barrel, up sharply from early October—driven by Middle East tensions that have threatened shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and disrupted supply. Refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, near full utilization, which means higher oil prices translate directly into better margins for refiners like Marathon.

The broader picture is that geopolitical risk has kept global oil prices elevated (world crude at $125.44 per barrel), and the International Energy Agency's warnings about market constraints have reinforced trader concerns about supply tightness. For a major refiner, this environment—high oil prices combined with strong refinery utilization—typically means strong profitability, which is what the stock's sustained climb over the past week reflects.
